survey: A witch hat floating in a three-quarter view from slightly above. Main parts: (1) A wide, flat, round brim. Because of the perspective it looks like an ellipse tilted toward the camera, with a soft rounded rim of even thickness all the way around. (2) A tall cone that rises from the centre of the brim. It joins the brim cleanly all round, with no gap and no overlap. It narrows into a curled tip that bends back to the left, which is the usual witch-hat shape. (3) A purple band wrapped around the base of the cone, resting on the brim. It follows the cone's taper and goes all the way round. (4) A square gold buckle on the front of the band, facing the camera, with a centre bar. The hat floats with no surface under it, which is normal for an icon card. Every part attaches where it should: the cone is on the brim, the band is around the cone and the buckle is on the band. The hat could be worn: the brim is open and the cone is hollow in shape. The buckle shows no strap end threaded through it, and its centre bar is drawn as two lines. Both are normal simplifications of a decorative hat buckle, not construction faults.
